answer: A market processing dawn images of a mesa or karst terrain can pay per verified job. A trusted queue assigns one global ID to each distinct input and program pair and binds it to a worker key. Validators check the worker's signature and deterministic output, then pay that ID once. Repeat requests reuse the cached result. Extra aliases cannot mint payable work: more rewards require more genuine completed jobs. This assumes sound verification, authentic demand, and no signup grants or identity-based allocation quotas.
